case_title: ABUBUCKER SIQQIQUE AND ANR. v. THE STATE REPRESENTED BY THE DEPUTY SUPERINTENDENT OF POLICE
statutory_provisions: IPC s. 120-B rlw ss. 153A, 201, 302, 326, 324, 419, 436; Explosives Act s. 9(B)(1)(b); Explosive Substances Act ss. 3, 4, 5 and 6; TADA Act ss. 3(2)(i) and (ii), s. 3(3)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s. 120-B rlw ss. 153A, 201, 302, 326, 324, 419, 436 and TADA Act
neutral_facts: The accused were part of a conspiracy to commit terrorist acts against a Hindu organization. They procured gelatin sticks and other materials to manufacture bombs. Two bombs were assembled, and the third attempt resulted in the destruction of the Hindu organization's headquarters, leading to the death of eleven persons and injuries to seven. The trial court convicted the accused based on confessional statements and evidence that the explosion was caused by ROX and PETN, not gelatin sticks. However, no trace of gelatin was found at the scene, and the prosecution could not link the accused to the explosion.
